files.purpose: The Settings window's root view and most of its pages. SettingsView (91-294) lays out a 780x580 window with a 212-point sidebar whose search field filters the ten SettingsPage cases by title and keywords, and a detail sheet whose top chrome row carries per-page capsules (model search, MCP server search, providers refresh, archive Delete all, About update accessory). An empty Archive shows a lone 44-pt "archivebox" symbol in place of the page. The file also declares the SettingsPage enum (title, SF Symbol, tint, keywords per page), the SettingsNavigation singleton that lets the update notification and the post-install relaunch open About, and the private page views: General, Appearance with AppZoomCard and BackdropOpacitySlider, Providers (one collapsible section per provider with status, usage, API key, binary path, install and sign-in rows), Source control, Archive, and About (credits, a licenses popover, a Made by Droppy row). The helpers are ProjectMarksRow and ThemePickerButton. In B3 the provider section's disclosure header is delegated to the shared CollapsibleProviderHeader.

side_effects: Writes AppSettings through bindings on every toggle and picker
Plays FinishChime when "Chime when a turn finishes" is switched on, SettleChime when "Sound when settling" is switched on
API key edits are saved via setAPIKeyInput, which the detail text says is stored in the Keychain, then after a 600 ms debounce the section runs providers.refresh and loadCatalog(force: true)
Binary path edits are saved via setBinaryPath
showsUsage turning true triggers refreshPlanLimits and refreshCredits (the registry throttles them to one read a minute)
Login opens a Terminal running provider.loginCommand; Reveal opens the worktrees directory in Finder
Restore unarchives; Delete and Delete all remove thread histories (with confirmation when confirmBeforeDeleting)
Links open getdroppy.app, credit repos, and provider install and key URLs
Reads LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md from the app bundle

feature_notes: B2->B3 is 2 insertions and 25 deletions in two hunks (churn 27). Mechanically verified: B2 :1-646 equals B3 :1-646, and B2 :671-1232 equals B3 :648-1209 apart from the card line, so every B2 cite at or after :671 moves up by exactly 23 and B2 :647-670 collapse onto B3 :647.

Hunk 1 (ProviderSettingsSection body, B2 :647-670 -> B3 :647). The 24-line inline disclosure Button is replaced by CollapsibleProviderHeader(provider: provider, isExpanded: $isExpanded, subject: "provider settings"). The struct is new in B3 at ModelsSettingsPage.swift:415-448 and is shared with the Models page (subject "model list", ModelsSettingsPage.swift:326). Its modifiers match the removed B2 code one for one, and its interpolated strings give the same B2 text: help "Hide the provider settings" / "Show the provider settings", accessibility hint "Shows or hides the provider settings", accessibility value "Expanded" / "Collapsed", label provider.displayName, isHeader trait. Nothing a user can see changes; it is a refactor.

Hunk 2 (ArchiveSettingsPage, B2 :921 -> B3 :898): `ChromeCard {` became `ChromeCard(lazy: true) {`. In B3, Chrome.swift's ChromeCard went from an unconditional LazyVStack to an eager VStack by default with an opt-in `lazy` flag ("Use lazy only for cards that list a long, uniform, growing collection."). This line keeps the archived-thread list lazy exactly as in B2. Every other ChromeCard in this file becomes eager in B3 through the Chrome.swift change, not through this file: the General, Appearance, AppZoomCard, per-provider, Source control and About cards.
No strings, settings keys, defaults, pages, keywords, controls or actions were added, removed or reworded in this file between B2 and B3.
